CausalChain: NAFLD-induced metabolic stress -> Upregulation of FTO expression -> Demethylation of m6A sites on metabolic enzyme mRNAs (e.g., PKM2) -> Increased mRNA stability and translation -> Enhanced glycolysis and lipogenesis -> Accumulation of immunosuppressive metabolic byproducts -> Formation of an immunosuppressive microenvironment -> Promotion of liver carcinogenesis
Hypothesis: In NAFLD-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, elevated FTO activity drives a selective loss of m6A modifications on key metabolic regulator transcripts, leading to metabolic reprogramming and the creation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that together facilitate liver cancer progression.
Abstract: Recent studies have highlighted the pivotal role of N6‐methyladenosine (m6A) modifications and their regulators in liver carcinogenesis. Here, we propose that in the context of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), an upregulation of the m6A demethylase FTO leads to selective demethylation of mRNAs encoding metabolic enzymes, such as PKM2. This preferential loss of m6A marks increases the stability and translational efficiency of these transcripts, thereby reprogramming cellular metabolism towards enhanced glycolysis and lipogenesis. Such metabolic reprogramming not only fuels tumor cell growth but may also contribute to an immunosuppressive microenvironment via accumulation of metabolic byproducts that impair effective T cell responses. Thus, targeting FTO-mediated m6A modifications could provide a novel therapeutic entry point for NAFLD-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
